name: Adjectival Tough Construction
pattern: Clause[Subject:NPᵢ + be + PredComp:AdjP[Adj + to-infinitival Clause with non-subject gapᵢ]]

entry.name: Adjectival Tough Construction
entry.pattern: Clause[Subject:NPᵢ + be + PredComp:AdjP[Adj + to-infinitival Clause with non-subject gapᵢ]]

1.definition: Characterizes the matrix subject by evaluating an action involving it.
1.details: In their argument was impossible to follow, the argument is understood as the object of follow. A preposition can supply the gap instead. The infinitival may have its own subject with for. Compare Kim was anxious to follow the argument, where Kim is the understood subject of follow. The construction makes an evaluation about the matrix subject, which excludes dummy there on this reading.

examples.note: The argument is the understood object of follow.

examples.form: [His performance was easy to find fault with.]
examples.note: The gap is the object of with.

examples.form: [The instructions were hard for us to follow.]
examples.note: Constructed with an overt subject in the infinitival.

relatedConstructions.notes: An adjectival predicative follows the matrix be.
The existing time-away entry uses the tough frame as an objecthood diagnostic.

grounds.note: Identifies the adjective and infinitival pattern with evaluation of an entity through an action.

projection.target: The matrix subject supplies a non-subject argument of the infinitival. The infinitival can separately identify who undertakes the action.
projection.evidence: CGEL compares hollow and ordinary infinitivals and contrasts their subject restrictions. CASA records the difficult-to-answer pattern.

curious.title: Easy to follow, hard to find fault with
curious.summary: In some sentences the adjective judges the opening noun by what we do to it, as in impossible to follow.
curious.body:
In Their argument was impossible to follow, the argument is understood as the thing being followed, even though follow has no object after it. His performance was easy to find fault with works the same way: the performance is what we find fault with.

The sentence evaluates the opening noun by an action involving it. The action can even have its own doer, as in The instructions were hard for us to follow. Compare Kim was anxious to follow the argument, where Kim is the one who follows.

examples.text: [His performance was easy to find fault with.]
[The instructions were hard for us to follow.]

curious.try: Say Their argument was impossible to follow. What is understood as the thing being followed?

teacher.summary: For advanced classes, the tough construction, where the subject is understood as a non-subject of the infinitival.
teacher.explain: In the tough construction, the matrix subject is linked to a gap in the infinitival that is not a subject. In their argument was impossible to follow, the argument is the understood object of follow. A preposition can supply the gap instead (easy to find fault with). The infinitival may have its own subject introduced by for (hard for us to follow). The construction evaluates the matrix subject by an action involving it, and it excludes dummy there on this reading. Compare Kim was anxious to follow the argument, where Kim is the understood subject of follow.
teacher.terms: Tough construction is the usual name. This dictionary also uses hollow infinitival for the to-clause with a gap.

examples.text: [His performance was easy to find fault with.]
[The instructions were hard for us to follow.]

contrasts.text: Their argument was impossible to follow.
contrasts.note: The argument is the understood object of follow.

contrasts.text: Kim was anxious to follow the argument.
contrasts.note: Kim is the understood subject of follow.

watch_for: A learner might look for an object after follow in impossible to follow, when the subject is understood as the object.
A learner might read Kim was anxious to follow the argument like the tough pattern, when Kim is the one following.
teacher.activity: Give students tough-pattern sentences. They say what is understood as the object or prepositional object of the verb, then compare with anxious to follow.
